🕳️ Trial and error

Reward hacking

In simple words

When an AI finds a loophole that earns lots of reward without doing what its designers really wanted.

When an agent finds a way to get a high reward without doing what the people who designed the reward actually wanted. The AI isn't cheating on purpose: it does exactly what the reward measures, and the reward measured the wrong thing.

Example. In a 2016 experiment by OpenAI, an AI playing the boat-racing game CoastRunners was rewarded for points. It found it could score more by circling in a lagoon, hitting the same targets again and again, than by finishing the race.

Related words

  • RewardThe score an agent gets after an action, telling it how good the result was.
  • AgentAn AI that acts on its own to reach a goal: it notices what is happening, chooses an action and sees the result.
  • AI alignmentMaking sure an AI tries to do what people really intend and value, not just what they literally said.
